heading: INT. FUNERAL HOME - REPOSITORY ROOM - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. FUNERAL HOME - REPOSITORY ROOM - AFTERNOON
Folding chairs.
A coffee urn.
Framed photos on an easel.
The last guests are drifting toward the door.
MARGUERITE OKAFOR-LINDQVIST (60s, black dress) stands by the coffin, one hand resting on its edge.
Her son THEO (30s, loosened tie) collects paper cups.
Her daughter ASHA (20s, red-eyed) folds programs into her purse.
Her brother DESMOND (50s, rumpled suit) stares at the carpet.
Her aunt GERTRUDE (80s, cane, hat with a veil) sits very upright and says nothing.
And on the far side of the room, a younger woman waits near the guest book.
Marguerite sets down her handkerchief, crosses to the coffee urn, pours two cups, hands one to Desmond, then sits beside Gertrude.
Theo drops a cup into the trash.
Asha zips her purse.
The younger woman steps forward.
NINA ABERNATHY (30s, gray coat, hair tied back) pauses at the edge of the circle.
I'm so sorry. I didn't know whether I should come.
units.name: NINA

units.text: Everyone looks at her.
Marguerite sets down her cup.
Who are you?
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Nina. I worked with your husband.
units.name: NINA

units.text: I don't remember a Nina.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: I was the night shift.
units.name: NINA

units.text: Gertrude lifts her veil an inch, studies Nina, and lowers it again.
Thank you for coming.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: He talked about you often.
units.name: NINA

units.text: Marguerite nods.
She places a hand on Nina's arm, gently, and walks her to the door.
